story.headline: Apple Introduces Refreshed iMac Powered by M6 Silicon and Dual 16-Core Neural Engine
story.summary: Apple officially announced the new 24-inch iMac powered by the M6 processor featuring core-integrated Neural Accelerators. The updated machine delivers up to 5x faster on-device AI performance compared to previous generations.

keyTakeaways: Apple refreshed the 24-inch iMac with M6 silicon featuring up to a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU, and a dual 16-core Neural Engine.
According to Apple, on-device AI performance is up to 5x faster than the previous M4 model, with ray tracing and SSD transfer speeds doubling.

Pricing begins at $1,499 for the 10-core configuration, with pre-orders beginning October 28, 2026, and retail availability starting November 6, 2026.
draft.body:
On October 27, 2026, Apple announced an upgraded version of its all-in-one desktop computer, introducing the [iMac with M6](https://www.apple.com/imac/) silicon. The refreshed machine integrates hardware specifically tuned for local machine learning, combining dedicated Neural Accelerators inside each graphics core with a dual 16-core Neural Engine, which was first introduced on desktop in the Mac mini in August. Apple states that the architecture delivers up to 5x faster on-device artificial intelligence performance compared to the previous M4 generation, expanding local model processing for home, school, and creative desktop environments.

The hardware announcement arrived as part of Apple's staggered rollout of M6-generation systems, following the initial introduction of the silicon in the Mac mini and preceding the wider launch of updated pro systems, as reported by [MacRumors](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/27/apple-announces-new-imac-with-m6-chip-and-more/). While the external industrial design of the 24-inch chassis remains consistent with the previous version, the internal hardware transition modernizes computing throughput, internal storage bus speeds, and wireless communication standards.

## M6 Silicon and the Dual Neural Engine

The central architectural shift in the updated iMac is Apple's M6 processor. The silicon is offered in two tiers: a base configuration with a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, and an upgraded configuration pairing a 12-core CPU with a 12-core GPU. Based on Mac mini Geekbench results reported by MacRumors, the M6 is estimated to deliver up to around 40 percent faster CPU performance than the previous iMac with M4, while [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2298132/apples-imac-with-m6-arrives-promising-a-huge-leap-in-ai-performance/) reported Apple claiming up to 50 percent faster performance in Excel, and up to 2.5x faster in general productivity tasks than the M1 model.

For graphics and neural computing, the M6 GPU incorporates hardware-level Neural Accelerators within each core. Apple paired this GPU architecture with a dual Neural Engine containing two 16-core blocks, doubling the engine hardware present in earlier iterations. Unified memory bandwidth has expanded to 170GB/s, up from the 120GB/s ceiling on M4 configurations. Base models include 16GB of unified memory, with factory upgrade options for 24GB and 32GB.

Apple states that these architectural adjustments yield up to 2x faster graphics processing and up to double the gaming performance for hardware-accelerated ray tracing compared to the M4 iMac. In local artificial intelligence workflows—such as large language model prompt evaluation in applications like LM Studio—Apple reports gains reaching up to 5x faster performance compared to M4, and up to 12x faster performance when measured against the M1 iMac.

[[FIG1]]

## Display, Design, and Hardware Specifications

The external enclosure of the iMac retains the thin design of the previous model and the selection of seven colors: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. Visuals are driven by the familiar 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, which outputs 500 nits of brightness with support for the P3 wide color gamut. For spaces with challenging reflections, Apple also provides a nano-texture glass configuration, as detailed on the [official iMac specifications](https://www.apple.com/imac/).

Internal storage speeds have improved through the integration of PCIe 5.0 architecture. Apple claims the updated bus allows the new internal SSDs to reach read and write speeds up to twice as fast as the solid-state drives used in the M4 models. Factory storage capacities start at 256GB on the entry-level machine and scale up to 2TB.

Audio and video hardware remain focused on remote communication. The iMac features a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera that supports Desk View, designed to keep users centered during video conferences or present an overhead view of a physical desk. Audio capture is handled by a studio-quality three-microphone array featuring directional beamforming, while output is routed through a six-speaker sound system with force-cancelling woofers, tweeters, and Spatial Audio support for Dolby Atmos.

## N1 Wireless Chip and Expanded Connectivity

Connectivity across the desktop line has also shifted through the deployment of Apple's proprietary N1 wireless chip. As reported by [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/27/apple-launches-new-imac-with-powerful-m6-chip/), the N1 introduces Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support to the iMac, upgrading the previous generation's Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 standards to reduce latency and improve wireless data transfer rates.

Physical I/O depends on the chosen processor tier. The base 10-core M6 iMac includes two Thunderbolt 4 ports alongside a 3.5mm headphone jack. The higher-tier 12-core model expands rear connectivity to four Thunderbolt 4 ports. Both configurations support up to two external 6K displays simultaneously.

[[FIG2]]

Wired networking has also received an optional boost. While previous models relied on Gigabit Ethernet, the power supply for the M6 iMac can be outfitted with a 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port, delivering up to 2.5x faster wired throughput according to Apple. The 2.5Gb Ethernet connector is standard on the $1,699 tier and available as a $30 build-to-order option on the base model.

## macOS 27 and Local AI Integration

The iMac ships with macOS 27 Golden Gate, incorporating Apple Intelligence and updated system integrations. Apple highlights that on-device processing powers tools such as intelligent email searches and automated tab organization in Safari, though footnote 4 notes that features such as Siri AI and AFM 3 Cloud models in Shortcuts rely on server-side models rather than purely on-device processing. Local processing also extends to third-party tools such as Pixelmator Pro, Claude, and Affinity.

For features requiring broader compute power, the operating system routes complex queries through Private Cloud Compute, which Apple notes does not retain personal information or make user data accessible to the company. However, regional availability remains staggered: footnote 4 of the press release for Apple's [14-inch MacBook Pro launch](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/10/apple-introduces-the-new-14-inch-macbook-pro-with-m6/) specifies that Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS, without stating it is unavailable on macOS.

## Pricing, Configurations, and Availability

The base 24-inch iMac with M6 starts at $1,499 in the United States. This configuration features a 10-core CPU, a 10-core GPU, the dual 16-core Neural Engine, 16GB of unified memory, 256GB of SSD storage, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports.

The upgraded $1,699 configuration includes the 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU variant of the M6 chip, four Thunderbolt 4 ports, 16GB of unified memory, and the integrated 2.5Gb Ethernet adapter. Both tiers include color-matched accessories in the box: a Magic Keyboard with Touch ID, a Magic Mouse, a 143W power adapter, a power cord, and a USB-C charging cable. Orders with the nano-texture glass option also include an Apple polishing cloth.

Apple opens pre-orders for the new iMac on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time through the online Apple Store. In-store retail availability and customer deliveries begin on Friday, November 6, 2026.

faq.q: What are the main performance differences between the M6 iMac and the M4 model?
faq.a: Based on Geekbench results reported by MacRumors, the M6 iMac should offer up to around 40 percent faster CPU performance, while Apple claims up to 2x faster graphics performance, twice the SSD storage transfer speeds, and up to 5x faster on-device AI performance compared to the iMac with M4.

faq.q: How much does the updated 24-inch iMac with M6 cost?
faq.a: Pricing begins at $1,499 for the base model with a 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage. An upgraded tier with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, four Thunderbolt 4 ports, and 2.5Gb Ethernet is priced at $1,699.

faq.q: When is the iMac with M6 available to order?
faq.a: Pre-orders begin on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time, with official availability and shipping scheduled for Friday, November 6, 2026.

The M6 chip features up to a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and a dual 16-core Neural Engine.
The M6 GPU introduces dedicated Neural Accelerators inside each graphics core for the first time on iMac.
The dual 16-core Neural Engine was first introduced on desktop in the Mac mini in August.
Apple claims on-device AI performance is up to 5x faster than the previous M4 model.
Geekbench results reported by MacRumors estimate the M6 delivers up to around 40 percent faster CPU performance than the M4 iMac.
Apple claims the M6 iMac is up to 50 percent faster in Excel and up to 2.5x faster in productivity performance than the M1 model.
Unified memory bandwidth expands to 170GB/s, up from 120GB/s on M4 configurations.
Base configurations include 16GB of unified memory with upgrade options for 24GB and 32GB.
Apple claims up to 2x faster graphics processing and up to double the gaming performance for ray tracing compared to the M4 iMac.
Apple reports up to 5x faster on-device prompt processing in LM Studio compared to M4, and up to 12x faster than M1.
The iMac enclosure retains its previous design and seven color options: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver.
The display is a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display with 500 nits of brightness and P3 wide color support, with an optional nano-texture finish.
PCIe 5.0 support enables SSD read and write speeds up to twice as fast as the M4 generation.
Storage options start at 256GB and scale up to 2TB.
The iMac includes a 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View support.
Audio hardware includes a three-mic array with directional beamforming and a six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos support.
An Apple-designed N1 wireless chip provides Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support, upgraded from Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3.
The base 10-core configuration includes two Thunderbolt 4 ports, while the 12-core tier features four Thunderbolt 4 ports.
The iMac supports up to two external 6K displays simultaneously.
The power adapter can be configured with a 2.5Gb Ethernet port, which comes standard on the $1,699 tier and costs $30 on the base tier.
The iMac runs macOS 27 Golden Gate with Apple Intelligence.
Footnote 4 notes that certain Apple Intelligence features like Siri AI and AFM 3 Cloud models in Shortcuts rely on server-side models subject to daily usage limits.
Local processing extends to third-party tools such as Claude.
claims.fix: State instead that the Mac is optimized to run AI applications like Claude, rather than claiming Claude processes locally.
